newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-INDIA START AS UNDERDOGS IN SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA START AS UNDERDOGS IN SECOND TEST.

text.p: An upbeat Sri Lanka, fresh from notching up the highest ever total in test cricket, start as favourites in the second test against India at Colombo's Singalese Sports Club on Saturday.
A psychologically battered India will face an uphill task against Sri Lanka, who demolished the Indian bowling earlier this week by amassing 952 for six on a lifeless wicket in the drawn first test.
Opener Sanath Jayasuriya hit 340 and shared a world record partnership for any wicket in test cricket of 576 with Roshan Mahanama who scored 225.
India's misery was further compounded by sterling knocks by skipper Arunjna Ranatunga and his deputy Aravinda de Silva as Sri Lankan batsmen made the Indians toil for three full days in the field.

"We've had our ups and downs in cricket, but I think we have come back pretty well in the batting," said Ranatunga in somewhat of an understatement. "We are very competitive now, but we'll have to work hard at our bowling and try to win matches."
Unlike the R.Premadasa Stadium, where the pitch proved to be a bowler's nightmare, the SSC wicket is expected to give them enough assistance with its extra bounce and movement.
SSC has a better record when it comes to results. Six of the nine tests played there have ended decisively while the remaining three were drawn.

Sri Lanka have brought left-arm fast-medium bowler Sajeeva de Silva into their squad and they are considering playing five bowlers by including the fastish off-breaks of Kumara Dharmasena at the expense of batsman Mahela Jayawardena, who made a promising start to his test career with an innings of 66.

India will make a last minute choice between 21-year-old inexperienced fast-medium bowler Debasis Mohanty and left-arm spinner Nilesh Kulkarni, who took a wicket off his first delivery in test cricket last weekend.

Sri Lanka (from): Arjuna Ranatunga (captain), Sanath Jayasuriya, Marvan Atapattu, Roshan Mahanama, Aravinda de Silva, Mahela Jayawardena, Romesh Kaluwitharana, Chaminda Vaas, Ravindra Pushpakumara, Muthiah Muralitharan, Sajeeva de Silva, Kumara Dharmasena.

India (from): Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Nayan Mongia, Navjot Sidhu, Rahul Dravid, Mohammad Azharuddin, Saurav Ganguly, Anil Kumble, Rajesh Chauhan, Abey Kuruvila, Venkatesh Prasad, Nilesh Kulkarni, Debasis Mohanty.
UMPIRES: B.C. Cooray (Sri Lanka) and R.E. Koertzen (South Africa).
